QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_53

question.text: Which entities are permitted to participate in the exchange-traded interest rate derivatives market in India?

answer.text: Any person resident in India and non-residents including FPIs to the extent specified in RBI directions; regulated entities such as mutual funds participate subject to their respective regulator's terms and applicable position limits
Only scheduled commercial banks and primary dealers
Only FIIs and mutual funds with minimum AUM of Rs. 500 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports broad participation: any person resident in India is eligible, and non-residents (including FPIs) can participate to the extent specified in RBI directions. Regulated entities such as mutual funds participate subject to their respective regulator's terms and applicable position limits. The Trap: Describing FPIs as "residents" is inaccurate; their participation is permitted as non-residents under RBI directions. There is no Rs. 500 crore AUM gate, and access is not limited to banks/PDs or portfolio managers alone. Note: Participation is jointly governed by RBI directions (for non-residents) and the respective regulator's rules for regulated entities, along with applicable position limits.
